about: Dated occupations and wartime annexations that the recognised borders of CShapes do not show. 'rows' re-tint an existing outline: the territory called 'names' on the map of that year, or, when that territory is not on the map (the Baltic states after 1940), the CShapes outline named in 'shape' as it stood on the given date; these are whole countries, and where only a part was occupied the note says so. A row with 'ohm' is drawn from the outline of that boundary relation in OpenHistoricalMap (public domain, CC0): Manchukuo inside China ('within'). 'areas' draw the occupied part of a country from Cliopatria (CC BY 4.0), which has one outline per calendar year of everything a power held: tools/build_occupations.py cuts the outline of 'clio' to each country in 'over' as CShapes draws it that year (and takes away the OpenHistoricalMap outline in 'minus_ohm'), between the dates given; 'covers' names rows whose own outline that part replaces. Cliopatria does not say which day of the year an outline stands for, and fronts moved within a year. Dates are the commonly cited ones from the Wikipedia article in 'source'. 'verified' is set by tools/build_occupations.py when the Wikidata item of that article has the same start and end years.

rows.label: Poland
rows.note: Germany invaded on 1 September 1939 and the Soviet Union on 17 September; the Soviet Union held the east until the German attack of June 1941. The Red Army drove the German forces out between July 1944 and early 1945. The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Czechoslovakia
rows.note: Bohemia and Moravia became a German protectorate on 15 March 1939; Slovakia was a German client state; the Sudetenland had been annexed in October 1938. The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Austria
rows.note: Annexed into Germany (the Anschluss) on 12 March 1938; a provisional Austrian government was set up on 27 April 1945. CShapes keeps the pre-war border.

rows.label: Norway
rows.note: The fighting in Norway lasted until 10 June 1940.

rows.label: Netherlands
rows.note: The south was freed in the autumn of 1944.

rows.label: Belgium
rows.note: Most of the country was freed in September 1944.

rows.label: France
rows.note: After the armistice of 22 June 1940 Germany occupied the north and the Atlantic coast; the south was governed from Vichy until German and Italian troops occupied it as well in November 1942. Paris was freed on 25 August 1944. The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Yugoslavia
rows.note: The country was divided between the Axis powers and their client states (the Independent State of Croatia). The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Greece
rows.note: Crete fell on 1 June 1941; Athens was freed on 12 October 1944.

rows.label: Hungary
rows.note: Hungary was a German ally until German troops occupied it on 19 March 1944.

rows.label: Estonia
rows.note: The Soviet Union had occupied and annexed Estonia in 1940; CShapes draws it inside the Soviet Union in these years, so its 1939 outline is used.

rows.label: Latvia
rows.note: The Soviet Union had occupied and annexed Latvia in 1940; German forces held Courland until May 1945. Its 1939 outline is used.

rows.label: Lithuania
rows.note: The Soviet Union had occupied and annexed Lithuania in 1940. Its 1939 outline is used.

rows.label: Iran
rows.by: the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union

rows.label: Iceland
rows.by: the United Kingdom, then the United States
rows.note: British troops landed on 10 May 1940; United States forces took over from July 1941.

rows.label: Ethiopia
rows.note: Annexed into Italian East Africa after the war of 1935 and 1936; Emperor Haile Selassie returned on 5 May 1941.

rows.label: Malaya
rows.note: Singapore fell on 15 February 1942.

rows.label: Burma
rows.note: Rangoon fell on 8 March 1942 and was retaken on 3 May 1945.

rows.label: French Indochina
rows.note: Japanese troops were stationed in the north from September 1940 and in the south from July 1941; the French administration stayed in place until the Japanese coup of 9 March 1945.

rows.label: Manchukuo (north-east China)
rows.note: Japan seized Manchuria after the Mukden Incident of September 1931 and proclaimed the state of Manchukuo on 1 March 1932, with the last Qing emperor Puyi at its head; Jehol was added in 1933. It was run by the Japanese Kwantung Army, most countries did not recognise it, and it ended with the Soviet invasion of August 1945. The outline is OpenHistoricalMap's.

rows.label: Austria
rows.by: the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom and France (Allied occupation)

rows.label: Belgium
rows.note: All but a strip behind the Yser was occupied. The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Romania
rows.note: Bucharest fell on 6 December 1916; about two thirds of the country was occupied while the government held Moldavia. The whole country is hatched: the sources have no shape for the occupied part alone.

rows.label: Iraq
rows.by: the United States and its coalition
rows.note: Baghdad fell on 9 April 2003; the Coalition Provisional Authority handed power to an Iraqi government on 28 June 2004.

over.name: Soviet Union
over.label: the occupied west of the Soviet Union
over.note: Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941. The hatched area is everything Cliopatria gives to Germany inside the Soviet Union in this calendar year (one outline per year; the front moved within each year, to Stalingrad and the Caucasus in late 1942 and back to the 1941 border by the end of 1944).

over.name: France
over.label: the occupied zone of France
over.note: Under the armistice of 22 June 1940 Germany occupied the north and the Atlantic coast, and the government at Vichy kept the south until German and Italian troops moved in on 11 November 1942. The hatched area is what Cliopatria gives to Germany inside France in this calendar year; Alsace-Lorraine, annexed in practice, is part of it.

over.name: China
over.label: the occupied parts of China
over.note: Japan invaded China proper in July 1937 and by late 1938 held the north China plain, the lower Yangtze and the main ports; its 1944 offensive (Ichi-Go) opened a corridor to Indochina. The hatched area is what Cliopatria gives to Japan inside China in this calendar year, without Manchukuo, which is listed separately; Japanese control outside the cities and railways was often thin.

over.name: France
over.label: occupied northern France
over.note: After the battles of 1914 the front ran from the Channel to Switzerland, and Germany held most of ten departments of northern and eastern France until 1918. The hatched area is what Cliopatria gives to Germany inside France in this calendar year (it has none for 1914).

over.name: Russia
over.label: the occupied west of Russia
over.note: In the Great Retreat of 1915 Russia lost Poland, Lithuania and Courland to Germany and Austria-Hungary; after the treaty of Brest-Litovsk (3 March 1918) German troops also occupied Ukraine, Belarus and the Baltic provinces until November 1918. The hatched area is what Cliopatria gives to Germany inside Russia, as CShapes draws it, in this calendar year.
